items.title: Catherine, Princess of Wales, Documents Life With Cancer in BBC Film
items.summary: “Cancer does change you,” Catherine, who is in remission, says in a trailer for the film. It will be released this month.

items.title: A Punk Rocker’s Painful Wait for Wheelchair Repairs
items.summary: Two private equity-backed companies now dominate the U.S. wheelchair market. For users, extended repair times can be dangerous and frustrating.

items.title: Top Drug Kingpin Is Captured by Mexican Army as Gunfire Erupts
items.summary: The arrest of Fausto Isidro Meza Flores, who is known as El Chapo Isidro and was one of the F.B.I.’s 10 most wanted, was a victory for the Mexican government.

items.title: Zelensky says Crimean Bridge strikes 'fair response' as he meets UK's Streeting
items.summary: Ukraine's president says Kyiv acted after 109 separate Russian aerial attacks on bridges in Ukraine.

items.title: On the Trail With Spain’s Prime Minister, as He Tries to Pull Out a Win
items.summary: Pedro Sánchez, Europe’s most prominent left-wing leader, seems set to lose power in an election next week. Our reporter trailed his last-ditch effort to turn his campaign around.

items.title: Cold gives way to rain in parts of UK as weather warning issued for south-west England
items.summary: Flood alerts in place and risk of power cuts as more than 100mm predicted to fall on Dartmoor on Sunday Cold snaps are to make way for heavy rain in some parts of the country as the Met Office issued a weather warning for south-west England. It said there will be a slow-moving band of rain moving across Devon and Cornwall, with more than 100mm due to fall on Dartmoor. Continue reading...

items.title: Reform UK considers pact with Restore Britain to overcome stalling performance in polls
items.summary: Thursday’s byelection in Castle Bromwich will be latest test for Nigel Farage’s party as rival eats into support Voters go to the polls in the village of Castle Bromwich in the West Midlands on Thursday in a little-noticed election that is the latest test for Reform at a time when it is particularly vulnerable. Yet, while it is the Conservatives who are edging ahead in recent polls, the decisive difference could well be the performance of Restore Britain – the…

items.title: Rejoining EU ‘on the table’ as UK makes deals on trade and young people
items.summary: All options open in future talks, says Ed Miliband, while prime minister hails ‘a good day for Britain and Europe’ The UK rejoining the EU could be on the table in informal discussions between Andy Burnham and European leaders in Brussels, Ed Miliband has said. The foreign secretary said “all options” would be examined in the process, after the prime minister agreed deals on trade and young people with the bloc on Friday. Continue reading...

items.title: Haitians excited but uneasy as El Salvador troops fight gangs
items.summary: Foreign combatants in Port-au-Prince welcomed by many after years of gang control but some fear offensive could exacerbate volatile situation A bullet-peppered mural of the Haitian striker Emmanuel Sanon covers the facade of Port-au-Prince’s main football ground. But more than two years have passed since any sports stars graced the pitch. In 2024, as the surrounding city was almost entirely captured by heavily armed gangs, Sylvio Cator stadium – where football greats including Brazil’s Ronaldo and Roberto Carlos once played…

items.title: Sarah McBride, Barred From Capitol Bathrooms, Wins Top Post
items.summary: Republicans have targeted the Delaware Democrat, the first openly transgender member of Congress, since she came to Washington. Her party just elevated her to a key job.

items.title: A Chicago Park Is Infested With Rats. Is a Wealthy Couple to Blame?
items.summary: People keep spreading nuts in a Chicago park, attracting rodents and neighbors’ fury. Officials are not sure how to stop it.

items.title: The California Grandparents Accused of Killing Jonathan McKinsey, Their Son-in-Law
items.summary: Jonathan McKinsey, 40, was gunned down in a suburban park after spending time with his three children. His wife’s parents have been charged with murder.

items.title: International Student Enrollment Plunged. Schools Are Bracing for More Losses.
items.summary: A blitz of new Trump administration policies are set to upend the lives of international students again, making it harder for them to live and work in the United States.

items.title: Fight over fossil fuels leaves COP31 climate talks in deadlock
items.summary: Countries from nearly 200 countries are in a deadlock to try and get a new global climate agreement.

items.title: FBI reportedly investigating apparent hack of its criminal database
items.summary: The National Crime Information Center database is used by federal and local law enforcement to share information.

items.title: Letby trial doctor barred from treating patients was expert witness in another case
items.summary: Prof Peter Hindmarsh played key role in conviction of two Birmingham parents whose son died after diabetes episode A doctor who gave expert evidence that helped to convict Lucy Letby, and who was barred during the trial from treating patients, was then instructed as an expert witness in another prosecution. The Guardian revealed this week that Prof Peter Hindmarsh was excluded from clinical practice in March 2023, during the main trial of Letby, by his employer, University College London hospitals…

items.title: Campaigners back call for scrutiny of consent laws by Joanne Young
items.summary: Experts say no law states third-party consent is a valid defence and call for public debate and further education Campaigners have welcomed a call for scrutiny of consent laws by a survivor of drug-facilitated rape but said action must also focus on wider issues around sexual assault. Joanne Young, who was drugged and raped by her husband and sexually abused by men he invited into their home, warned of “serious questions about how the law deals with consent”. Continue reading...

items.title: Federal Court Halts Pregnant Workers’ Protection Law
items.summary: The Fifth Circuit Court of Appeals said the law was unconstitutional because it was passed with proxy voting during the Covid pandemic. It is expected to be appealed to the Supreme Court.

items.title: In France’s Angry Autumn, TV News Channels Are Accused of Stirring the Pot
items.summary: Critics say that CNews and BFM TV, two major news channels, have used racist language in protest coverage. The channels deny it.

items.title: Man convicted of starting Palisades fire in Los Angeles
items.summary: The 30-year-old LA resident was convicted of arson leading to wildfires that killed 12 people and destroyed more than 6,800 buildings.
